newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-FENUKITAU SINKS CANTERBURY WITH TRY HAT-TRICK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FENUKITAU SINKS CANTERBURY WITH TRY HAT-TRICK.

text.p: Former Tongan international flanker Ipolito Fenukitau scored a hat-trick of second-half tries as the Australian Capital Territory Brumbies steam-rollered Canterbury Crusaders 49-29 in a Super 12 match on Saturday.
Although ACT delighted the crowd at Bruce Stadium by running in six tries, it was the accurate kicking of David Knox that gave the home side such a commanding margin of victory.

The former Australia fly-half kicked five conversions and landed two penalties and a drop goal for a personal haul of 19 points as ACT recorded their second victory in four outings in the southern hemisphere provincial competition.
"If we play like that we can beat anyone. Our second half performance was magnificent," Knox enthused afterwards.
Canterbury scored five tries themselves but only managed to add two conversions from the boot of flyhalf Leon MacDonald.
The Brumbies collected four points for the victory while both sides picked up a bonus point for scoring more than four tries in the match.
Fenukitau's three tries put the game beyond Canterbury's reach after a tight first half which saw ACT lead by just three points 13-10.

The visitors, in fact, had started the brighter with tries from wingers Paula Bale and James Kerr. ACT took the lead on the stroke of half-time when Wallaby scrumhalf George Gregan dived over from close range and Knox converted.

But when lock forward John Langford and winger Mitch Hardy added to Fenukitau's tries in the second half, the Brumbies romped into a 46-10 lead before the visitors regained some pride with tries through flanker Scott Robertson and centre Tabai Matson, who scored twice.
